INTRODUCTIONM
This lesson will help you understand basic high frequency (HF) systems.
High frequency (HF) systems, like any other radio system, transmit and receive voice and data using the earth's atmosphere as the transmission medium.
Due to the HF system's ability to communicate over long distances and over the horizon, day or night, it is used by, but not limited to, the military, mariners, and air traffic control centers.

High power transmitters are used in HF systems to ensure that the transmission will be strong enough for the receiver to detect clearly.
HF system receivers have high sensitivity. The higher the receiver's sensitivity, the greater the ability to receive weak signals.

Conditions in the ionosphere have a great effect on HF transmissions. When transmitted frequencies enter the ionosphere, they are refracted back to the earth's surface, creating an area of radio silence called a skip zone. amount of refraction depends on; the density of the ionosphere, the frequency, and the angle that the radio wave enters the ionosphere. $Back: P10011111
The amount of refraction depends on the density of the ionosphere, the frequency, and the angle at which the radio wave enters the ionosphere.

Ionosphere - is part of the earth's atmosphere. It extends approximately between 50 and 250 miles above the earth's surface. The ionosphere is broken into layers (D, E and F). The layers contain negative ions, positive ions and free electrons.
DEFINITION

The density of the ionosphere is changed by the sun's radiation. During daylight hours the sun's radiation strikes the ionosphere and it becomes denser and closer to the earth's surface. This increases refraction and reduces the size of the skip zone...
In the evening, less of the sun's radiation strikes the ionosphere and it becomes less dense and farther from the earth's surface. This decreases refraction and increases the size of the skip zone.

The skip zone either lengthens or shortens the HF system's communication distance. To compensate for the skip zone, the radio operator can adjust the HF system frequency. This adjustment can lengthen or shorten the communication distance, maintaining 24-hour connectivity between transmitter and receiver.....
Higher frequencies are required during the daylight hours when the density of the ionosphere is increased by the sun's radiation. Refraction increases and the skip zone decreases..

Lower frequencies are used during the evening and at night when the density of the ionosphere decreases. Refraction decreases and the skip zone increases. Lower frequencies will hop and propagate at longer distances because less power is absorbed by the ionosphere....

HF system operators remember this rule of thumb to determine which way to adjust the frequency for optimum communications: The higher the sun, the higher the frequency. The maximum frequency that each ionosphere layer will refract is known as the Critical frequency...
Some frequencies will pass through the ionosphere into space, while others are refracted back towards earth. The highest angle that allows radio waves to refract is called the Critical angle.
The Critical angle is determined by the height of the ionosphere and the frequency of the transmitted signal. Again, a frequency adjustment is made to achieve successful communication.

HF systems have four basic modes of operation.n............

Amplitude Modulation (AM) mode transmits the carrier and both sidebands (USB and LSB). Large amounts of transmitting power are consumed in transmitting both sidebands. This causes a large bandwidth and decreases the peak transmitted talk power...
Amplitude Modulation Equivalent (AME) is a process that HF receiver transmitters use. The carrier is re-inserted with the sideband prior to transmission creating an AME signal.
Upper Side Band (USB) is the most common mode of operation. This is a Single Side Band (SSB) transmission that removes both the carrier and LSB prior to transmission.

USB signals are more efficient than AM because all transmit power is concentrated into talk power. USB creates a smaller bandwidth and output power only occurs when the microphone is keyed and the user talks...
Lower Side Band (LSB) is similar to USB but uses the sideband below the carrier frequency. This example signal has been modulated by a 1 kHz tone. Note the transmit frequency is
1 kHz lower than the carrier frequency..

USB and LSB are two different frequencies. Long haul naval communications uses a variation of SSB called Independent sideband (ISB) transmission. ISB uses outputs from two sideband generators; filtering and combining the USB and LSB into one envelope containing different intelligence on each sideband....

Antenna lengths can be reduced by quarter wavelengths and still maintain impedance matching for a given frequency. However, an antenna coupler can be used to electrically change the length of the antenna to allow a large bandwidth of frequencies to use the same antenna...
The antenna coupler connects the receiver transmitter to the HF antenna. It matches the appropriate electrical antenna length to the selected frequency.

Common HF antenna couplers accomplish the following tasks: lers electrically lengthen or shorten an antenna by adding inductors or capacitors in series. Couplers match the antenna impedance. Couplers monitor the Standing Wave Ratio (SWR)))
